beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code credentials or write the URI into logs or committed files.

Reuse a single MongoClient/MongoClient-like connection object across the app (create once at process start and share), and configure a connection pool (e.g. maxPoolSize) rather than opening a new connection per request.

Use TLS/SSL for all connections (connection string must include tls/ssl=true or use the mongodb+srv scheme), and restrict network access via firewall/VNet rules so only the app runtime IPs can reach the cluster.

Store documents with explicit fields needed for retrieval and citation: { _id, transcript_id, chunk_id, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, text, embedding: <float array>, metadata } so answers can always cite source transcript and timestamp.

Create a single collection (or logically separate collections) that stores the text chunk and its embedding in the same document so nearest-neighbor retrieval returns text and metadata without an extra lookup.

When chunking transcripts, use a predictable chunk size and overlap tuned for the LLM context window (e.g., 500–1000 tokens per chunk with 50–200 token overlap) and record chunk boundaries and timestamps in metadata so the RAG pipeline can assemble context and cite precisely.

Provision a vector-capable collection/index with parameters that match the embedding dimension: set vector index dims=384 (embedding model all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and choose the cluster-supported index type (e.g., vector-diskann or HNSW/IVF) and cosine similarity (metric=COS) when creating the index.
Also create conventional indexes on fields used for filtering or grouping (e.g., transcript_id, chunk_id, start_timestamp) to make filter-by-transcript or time-range queries efficient.

Store embeddings as an array of floats of length 384 (or the database-specific binary vector format expected by the engine) and document the exact vector shape and field name used so index creation and queries match.

Implement NN search using the cluster's vector search API/operator and restrict returned fields via projection (text, timestamps, transcript_id, score) to reduce bandwidth; ensure the vector search call includes 'topK' and an appropriate score threshold.
Apply metadata-based pre-filtering (e.g., transcript_id or date range) before or as part of vector search to reduce candidate set and improve precision for domain-specific queries.

Use projection and pagination: when scanning results fetch only needed fields and paginate/limit responses (e.g., limit topK to 10-50) so post-processing and LLM context assembly stays within memory and token limits.

Before inserting chunks, deduplicate by a deterministic key (e.g., transcript_id + chunk_id + checksum) or use upsert semantics so re-running ingestion is idempotent and does not create duplicate embeddings/index entries.
Use exponential backoff and retry for transient network errors and rate limits when calling the database or embedding model; make writes idempotent or use upserts so retries don't duplicate data.

Limit the vector dimensionality and ensure embedding model choice matches provisioned vector index dims to avoid incompatible insert/query errors (document the model name and dims=384 in README and .env.example).

Record provenance metadata per chunk (source filename, original page/line offsets, timestamp, ingestion time, embedding model used) and include those fields in query results to allow verifiable citations in LLM responses.

Monitor index and query performance (index build times, disk usage, query latencies, topK recall) and set alerts when vector index memory/disk pressure or query latencies exceed thresholds; use the MCP server tools to inspect created indexes and query plans.

When creating the vector index, pick and tune index-specific parameters (e.g., efConstruction, efSearch, M for HNSW or IVF/centroids settings) appropriate to DiskANN/HNSW/IVF index type and expected query throughput/recall tradeoffs.
Keep database-level credentials with least privilege for the sample: create a user scoped to the sample_fintech_04 database and avoid using a full-admin key in the sample's configuration.
Back up the database or enable provider-managed backups before bulk ingest or index builds; large vector indexes and bulk loads can be expensive to roll back.

In the RAG pipeline, assemble retrieved passages to fit the chosen LLM context window by scoring and truncation: rank retrieved chunks by vector score, then concatenate until token budget minus answer buffer is reached; prefer higher-score chunks from distinct timestamps to improve coverage.

Sanitize and normalize text before embedding (strip control characters, normalize whitespace, preserve timestamps) to ensure consistent chunking, reproducible embeddings, and better nearest-neighbor accuracy.

When verifying index creation and document inserts in automation, use the cluster's management/inspection tools (the DocumentDB MCP server helpers or equivalent) to fetch index definitions and validate document counts; treat any failure in those checks as a blocking issue for verification.
Avoid storing raw secret keys in code or repository examples; include a .env.example with placeholder DOCUMENTDB_URI and document how to set real values in environment variables or a secrets manager.

For performance and cost reasons, batch inserts of document+embedding (e.g., 100–1000 docs per bulk insert) rather than inserting one document at a time during ingestion, and monitor RU/throughput or equivalent credits during bulk loads.
